stem: A bank must pull change data from a database that sits inside its own data centre, using the platform's managed connector rather than bespoke code. The team is working out how many pipeline objects the standard pattern asks them to create.

option_texts.A: Two, an ingestion gateway plus an ingestion pipeline that references the gateway
option_texts.B: One, a single ingestion pipeline that reaches the database directly
option_texts.C: Two, a landing job that exports files plus a pipeline that reads them
option_texts.D: Three, one per medallion layer, each reading the database in turn

drill_answer_short: Gateway-based CDC uses two objects: an ingestion gateway, then an ingestion pipeline referencing the gateway id
decision_hinge: Standard CDC is gateway-based and uses two pipelines, an ingestion gateway and an ingestion pipeline: you create a gateway, then create an ingestion pipeline that references the gateway id.

plausible_options.B: using the platform's managed connector rather than bespoke code

eliminated_by.C: must pull change data from a database that sits inside its own data centre
eliminated_by.D: working out how many pipeline objects the standard pattern asks them to create

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - a single pipeline is the shape for sources that need no gateway
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - an export-and-read design is the bespoke code the bank is avoiding
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - the medallion layers are not one ingestion object each

stem: A team schedules its gateway-based ingestion to refresh every six hours and is budgeting the compute. They have to state how the gateway component behaves between those refreshes and who looks after its staging area.

option_texts.A: It starts with each refresh and leaves its staging area for the team to clear
option_texts.B: It runs continuously and manages its staging volume internally
option_texts.C: It runs continuously but needs the team to prune its staging area by hand
option_texts.D: It runs only once at setup, after which the pipeline reaches the source alone

drill_answer_short: The gateway runs continuously and manages the staging volume internally
decision_hinge: In gateway mode the gateway runs continuously, and the gateway manages the staging volume internally.

eliminated_by.C: who looks after its staging area
eliminated_by.D: schedules its gateway-based ingestion to refresh every six hours

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - the refresh cadence belongs to the pipeline, not to the gateway's lifetime
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - the staging volume is managed for you rather than pruned by hand
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - the gateway is not a one-off setup step

stem: A team wants to load a folder of files without first writing out every column and type by hand. They would rather the load statement work the shape out from the files themselves on the first run.

option_texts.A: Declare the full column list first, since a load statement cannot work a shape out
option_texts.B: Load into a single string column, then split it into typed columns afterwards
option_texts.C: Create an empty placeholder table and let the load infer the shape from the files
option_texts.D: Register the folder as an external table, which carries the shape with it

drill_answer_short: Create an empty placeholder Delta table so COPY INTO infers the schema from the source files
decision_hinge: You can create empty placeholder Delta tables so that the schema is inferred during a COPY INTO operation, which supports target table schema inference, mapping, merging, and evolution.

plausible_options.B: work the shape out from the files themselves on the first run

eliminated_by.A: without first writing out every column and type by hand
eliminated_by.D: A team wants to load a folder of files

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - the load statement does support schema inference
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - a string landing table defers the typing instead of inferring it
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling - an external table does carry a schema, but it is not a load of the files

stem: A pipeline has to take records from cloud object storage and from a message bus, appending each new record as it arrives. The team is picking which dataset kind the ingest step should declare.

option_texts.A: A materialized view, a dataset that recomputes its result on each pipeline refresh
option_texts.B: A temporary view, which holds the arriving records for the next step to read
option_texts.C: An external table, which points at the arriving files where they already sit
option_texts.D: A streaming table, the primary dataset type for ingestion in a pipeline

drill_answer_short: Streaming tables are the primary dataset type for ingestion, from object storage via Auto Loader or from message buses
decision_hinge: Streaming tables are useful for ingesting data from cloud object storage using Auto Loader or from message buses like Kafka, and they are the primary dataset type for ingestion.

plausible_options.A: records from cloud object storage and from a message bus

eliminated_by.B: appending each new record as it arrives
eliminated_by.C: picking which dataset kind the ingest step should declare

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - a materialized view recomputes a result rather than appending arrivals
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - a temporary view holds no data between pipeline steps
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - an external table cannot consume a message bus

stem: A table's owner has left and a squad now needs a colleague granted read on that table. No one in the squad owns the table itself, and they are working out who is entitled to make the grant.

option_texts.A: The owner of the catalog or schema that contains the table may also grant
option_texts.B: Anyone holding read on the table, since a privilege may be passed along
option_texts.C: Only a workspace administrator, because ownership has lapsed with the departure
option_texts.D: Nobody until the table is recreated, because grants follow the original owner

drill_answer_short: Privileges can be granted by the object's owner or by the owner of the catalog or schema containing it
decision_hinge: Privileges can be granted by the owner of the object, or by the owner of the catalog or schema that contains the object.

plausible_options.C: No one in the squad owns the table itself

eliminated_by.B: a colleague granted read on that table
eliminated_by.D: they are working out who is entitled to make the grant

distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - holding a privilege does not confer the right to pass it on
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - admins do hold wide rights, but the containing owner is the entitled party here
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - grants do not die with the original owner
